chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn Bukayr al-Taweel, who said:

My father called me when death approached him, and he said: 'O my son! Take hold of the wealth of your younger brothers, conduct business with it, take half the profit for yourself, and give them the other half. And there is no guarantee (liability) upon you.'

So the mother who gave birth to my father (his concubine) brought me before Ibn Abi Layla after my father's death, and she said to him: 'This one is eating the wealth of my son.' I said, so I narrated to him what my father had ordered me with. Ibn Abi Layla said: 'If your father ordered you with falsehood, I would not approve of it.' Then Ibn Abi Layla established a witness upon me: 'If I move it, then I am responsible for it.'

So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) later, and I narrated to him my story, then I said to him: 'What do you see?' He said: 'As for the words of Ibn Abi Layla, I cannot refute them. And as for what is between you and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, there is no guarantee upon you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father entrusting his son with the wealth of minor siblings for trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia juristic distinction between *daman* (financial liability/guarantee) and *zikr* (accountability) in the management of orphans' wealth. While the judge Ibn Abi Layli validated the arrangement in a civil context, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the son bears no financial liability (*daman*) for losses, yet remains spiritually accountable (*zikr*) to God for his stewardship, highlighting the nuance between legal immunity and divine responsibility.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from Khalid Bin Bakeyr al Taweel who said,

‘My father called over when the death presented itself to him, so he said, ‘O my son! Take hold of the wealth of your younger brothers, so do some business with it and take half the profits (for yourself) and give them the (other) half. And the guaranteeing is not upon you’.

So the mother who gave birth for his father, after the death of my father, took me to Ibn Abu Layli, so she said to him, ‘This one is eating the wealth of my son’. So I related the story of what I had been ordered with by my father. So Ibn Abu Layli said, ‘If the father has ordered you with the falsehood, I would not allow it’. Then Ibn Abu Layli established a witness upon me that if I were to move it, so I would be held responsible for it’.

So I came up to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> afterwards, so I related to him<sup>asws</sup> my story, then I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What do you<sup>asws</sup> see?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the words of Ibn Abu layli, so I have no leeway of rejecting it, and as for what is in between you and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, so there is no responsibility upon you’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Khalid ibn Bukayr al- Tawil who has narrated the following:

“My father called me at the time of his death and said, ‘Son, take the assets of your small brothers and use them in business. Take half of the profit and give them the other half and you will not be held responsible.’

A mother of the child of my father took me, after the death of my father, before ibn abu Layla’ and said to him, ‘This person eats the property of my children.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘I then told my story that my father had commanded me to do.’ Ibn abu Layla’ said, ‘If your father commanded you to do what is unlawful, I cannot allow it.’ Ibn abu Layla’ appointed a witness (to bear testimony) that if I moved it I will be held responsible.

I then visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, later and told my story, then asked about his opinion. He (the Imam) said, ‘I cannot reject the words of ibn abu Layla’, however, between you and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, you are not responsible.’”
